title: ChatEvent
description: One line of events.jsonl and one server-sent event. Bodies reuse feature 001 review-session definitions. Amended by feature 014: usage optionally carries served_model and retries, and error optionally carries stop_reason and retries; older bodies remain valid.

send_when_checked.description: Feature 015: present only for a review started with the box unticked.

carried_withdrawals.description: Feature 015 cycle 12 (owner decision 193A, extended to Check again; its FR-029): present only on a re-run's start whose earlier record withdrew findings with a decision: each such withdrawal's finding.withdrawn body, as the earlier record's report.md names it - those it carried itself first - in the order they went. Their ids are the earlier record's, so a reader drops no finding for them; report.md names them under 'Withdrawn with a decision' before this session's own. A fold's withdrawal names nothing and is never carried. Amended 2026-11-02 (cycle 12's Codex review): each item also names session_id, the session that withdrew it - the earlier record's for its own withdrawals, kept as it was for one that record carried itself - since finding ids restart in each session; report.md names it on the item's line. Amended 2026-11-03 (feature 002 cycle 16): an item keeps the title of the body it carries, when that body names one, which report.md names right after the id.

basis.description: Feature 013 (contracts/sources.md section 3): the answer basis, computed by code from the steps the answer's turn recorded since the last answer - how many results it read, and whether the review read any drawing - never from the model's text. The runner adds it to every text.done of a review turn; the page prints it after the AI guidance chip, before the answer. Optional: an older text.done has none.

body.description: Amended 2026-11-02 (feature 002 cycle 13; FR-031): the finding, closed here rather than in its definition, and beside it, while some finding records a triage, the review's triage tally as the session then stands - the finding in it, or the fold that announces it done - as the disposition events carry it. The Review page shows it as it arrives, so a finding a resumed turn adds is counted at once; a body with none hides a shown one, as theirs does. Amended 2026-11-02 (cycle 13's Tier 2 review): the backend names the key on every finding body, null while no finding records a triage, and the page changes the tally only when a finding body names the key, null hiding it, so an older backend's finding, which has no key, leaves the tally as it was (009 FR-030).

Feature 013 (contracts/part-roles.md section 9): the finding left the session, because a check restated after the engineer answered no longer produces it - a part answered bought is not graded. Emitted by ToolContext.withdraw_findings, the one place a finding leaves the session, once per finding in session order. A reader of the stream drops the finding with this id; an id it does not hold is ignored. Amended 2026-11-01 (feature 002 cycle 6; FR-031): the runner also withdraws the id a re-run or restated finding was first announced under once it folds onto an earlier finding's id, right before the finding event announcing it under that id, and names that id as folded_into. Its verdict stands under folded_into, so a reader that counts withdrawn verdicts passes over it; one that drops the id it names is right as before. Amended 2026-11-02 (feature 002 cycle 10; roadmap hole H-g-010; FR-031): a finding that held a decision takes it with it, and its withdrawal names what it took - disposition and taken, both or neither. A fold's withdrawal, and an undecided finding's, carry neither: a fold's decision stands under folded_into, or its disposition.cleared says what the fold took.

title.description: Feature 002 cycle 16 (FR-031): the finding's display title, as its finding event names it - whole, its parts named - which the backend names on every withdrawal it writes: an answer's, a decision taken or not, and a fold's, the title of the finding event it announces next. report.md's withdrawn lines, a read-only restore's lines and the Review page's Transcript name it in parentheses right after the id. Optional: an older body has none, and its line is printed as before.

folded_into.description: Feature 002 cycle 6: present only on a fold's withdrawal, the id the folded finding took.

disposition.description: Feature 002 cycle 10 (roadmap hole H-g-010): present only when the finding held a decision: the disposition that went with it, as the session last held it.

taken.description: Feature 002 cycle 10 (roadmap hole H-g-010): present with disposition alone: the words file's clause naming the decision and, when one was recorded, its triage - a pass's wrong as a miss, as its card words it - such as 'your Reject (wrong) went with it'. The Review page's Transcript ends the withdrawal's line with it, after the reason, as sent, and report.md prints the same line under 'Withdrawn with a decision'.

triage_tally.description: Feature 002 cycle 7 (FR-031): the review's triage tally as this decision left it, present only while some finding records a triage. The disposition route's reply carries the same beside the finding.

body.description: Feature 002 (owner decisions 189A and 191A; FR-031): a check the model ran again after an answered evidence request resumed its turn folded onto a decided finding (rule 3) with another verdict - another status or severity - so the finding's disposition was cleared. Emitted by the runner after the fold's finding event for the same id, once per finding, in session order. disposition is the one cleared; reason is the words file's line naming its decision and triage, which the page prints on the finding's card. A re-run with the status and severity decided keeps the disposition, and nothing is emitted. Amended 2026-11-01 (owner decision 194A): the runner emits it too when a check restated after an answer (58A's restate) folds onto a decided finding with another status or severity, after that fold's finding event, and when a re-run of a waiting review does not carry a decision onto the finding with its subject key because that finding's status or severity changed (feature 015's carry), naming that finding; reason then names the restate or the carry. Owner decision 193A: both snapshots name, under cleared, each undecided finding's last such body. Amended 2026-11-02 (feature 015 cycle 12; 193A extended to Check again): a re-run's carry also writes, before any decision it carries, each undecided earlier finding's last such body from the earlier record's own stream, naming the one finding with its subject key, its disposition and reason as they were and its triage_tally the review's. Amended 2026-11-02 (feature 015 cycle 12's Tier 1 review, recorded on its read-only check): it writes one only onto a finding at the status and severity of the earlier finding it was written on, where its reason, that this verdict changed, still holds; elsewhere it writes none.

triage_tally.description: Feature 002 cycle 7 (FR-031): the review's triage tally as the clear left it, present only while some finding records a triage. Amended 2026-11-01 (cycle 7's Tier 2 review): a restate withdraws the findings it no longer produces before it sends its notices, so each counts what the restate leaves; and a snapshot's cleared lines leave the tally out, since a later decision may have outdated it - a snapshot's one tally is its summary's.

body.description: Feature 011 T092: every coverage item of these checks left each of these buckets, before the check restated its state. Emitted by ToolContext.withdraw_coverage, the one place an announced item leaves the session, and only when an item did; each check and each bucket once, in the order given. A reader of the stream drops the items whose check is in checks and whose bucket is in buckets, so it holds what the session holds; nothing identifies one coverage item with another.

What one model round trip cost, emitted by the adapter once per request (feature 005). Every token count is nullable because a field the endpoint omitted is unknown, not zero, and the two providers' sub-counts nest differently and are never summed across them. The original fields remain required; feature 014's served_model and retries are optional so older bodies remain valid.

round_index.description: The adapter's own per-turn counter, zero-based and reset each turn, the convention tool.started.step_index already uses. No turn number is carried: turns are delimited by the turn.ended events

tool_result_input_tokens.description: Gemini only; the same tokens are already inside input_tokens on OpenAI

latency_s.description: Wall clock of the one request, measured by the adapter. Never null

cache_diagnostic.description: OpenAI's prompt-cache outcome for this round, recorded verbatim; null on Gemini, null on fake, and null on OpenAI whenever prompt_cache_options.comparison_response_id was not sent

served_model.description: Feature 014: the model id the provider reports answered this round, omitted when it reported none

retries.description: Feature 014: the failed tries before this round's request succeeded, written only under a retry policy, which only benchmark attempts set

usage.description: What the session cost, summed under the one rule SessionUsage defines, so the pane does not own a second one (feature 005). Optional: absent when no round reported usage, and absent on every stream written before this feature

stop_reason.description: Feature 014: a stop the provider itself reported, a Gemini finish reason, an OpenAI incomplete reason or failure code, context_length_exceeded or input_token_limit

retries.description: Feature 014: the tries made for the request that failed, written only under a retry policy

TriageTally.description: Feature 002 cycle 7 (FR-031; owner decisions 185A and 187A): how the triage stands - the flagged findings, every status but checked_within_scope, by outcome (counts) and with none (not_recorded), and the passes judged wrong, the misses - with report.md's By triage and misses lines for them (text, misses_text), counted by report/summary.triage_tally, the one rule those lines come from. The review summary carries it as triage_tally too. The Review page prints the two lines as sent. Settled 2026-11-02: an event's tally is the count when that event is sent - after a restate settles, after a fold, or after each decision a re-run's carry carries or clears - so a decision carried later is not in an earlier notice's count, and the last notice of a Check again's carry counts what the carry leaves.
